title: Post-CABG Acute Low Cardiac Output — Isolated RV Failure

patient.name: John Doe
history: Prior MI x2 (DES placed 3 years ago)
patient.procedure: CABG x3, left atrial appendage (LAA) closure / MAZE — no significant intraoperative events

stages.label: Baseline — POD0, arrival from OR
stages.facilitatorNotes: Fresh off bypass, already on epinephrine 3 mcg/min. Note the pattern before anything changes: CVP 18 is elevated while PA systolic/diastolic (28/14) is comparatively unremarkable — the right ventricle, not the left, is the problem. Encourage the learner to look at CVP vs. PA diastolic relationship rather than just reacting to the low CI.

stages.label: Stage II — Unaddressed RV Failure Progression
stages.facilitatorNotes: Chest tube output stays flat (~40 mL) — reinforces this isn't bleeding/tamponade. Correct next moves: start milrinone (± inhaled nitric oxide — not a modeled numeric field in this engine, track it as a debrief marker) to unload/support the RV. Two traps: a fluid bolus (CVP is already high — this worsens RV distension) and more epinephrine (SVR is already elevated — this raises RV afterload further).

stages.label: Facilitator checkpoint — was RV-directed therapy initiated appropriately?

branches.label: Learner initiated milrinone (± inhaled nitric oxide), avoided fluid bolus and additional epinephrine
Fluid bolus and/or additional epinephrine given, or RV-directed therapy not started

stages.facilitatorNotes: Pick based on what actually happened at the bedside — this isn't timed, it's your call as the facilitator.

stages.label: Improving — Milrinone Response

successCriteria.label: Considered/initiated inhaled nitric oxide for RV afterload reduction
Avoided fluid bolus despite low CO, recognizing elevated filling pressures

stages.facilitatorNotes: Milrinone onset ~5 minutes. Once settled, manually advance to the debrief discussion stage — no auto-advance here, this is the good outcome, let it breathe before debriefing.

stages.label: Debrief — Weaning & Recovery Planning
stages.prompt: The patient's hemodynamics have stabilized on milrinone. What's the plan from here — when and how do we start weaning milrinone, and what tells us this patient is ready to move toward extubation?
stages.note: Milrinone wean: typically down-titrated slowly once CI/CVP/UOP have been stable for a sustained period, watching for rebound in filling pressures or a drop in CI as the dose comes down — trend-driven, not a fixed timeline. Extubation readiness: hemodynamic stability off escalating support, adequate gas exchange, chest tube output trending down and non-bleeding, appropriate neuro wake-up. Good prompt for the learner: what would make you hesitant to wean right now, given this patient's RV was the primary problem?

stages.label: Worsening — Progressive Cardiogenic Shock
stages.facilitatorNotes: Watch the strip — increasing ventricular ectopy (frequent PVCs) is the real-world warning sign preceding pulseless VT; this engine doesn't model ectopy burden as a distinct field, so narrate it live rather than expecting it on the monitor. Last chance to correct course: stop fluid/epi escalation, start milrinone now.

stages.label: Cardiac Arrest — Pulseless Ventricular Tachycardia
stages.facilitatorNotes: A mechanically-driven arrest — the underlying problem is still RV failure, not a primary electrical event. Run the code live from the Console (shock/CPR/ROSC are live facilitator actions, not scripted here). Debrief point once resolved: the rhythm might convert, but did the RV problem actually get addressed, or just the arrest?
